units.sourceHTML: 3.6 Basic vs Extended Regular Expressions

units.text: Basic regular expressions differ from extended regular expressions in the following ways:
units.sourceHTML: Basic regular expressions differ from extended regular expressions in the following ways:

units.text: The characters ‘⟦0⟧’, ‘⟦1⟧’, ‘⟦2⟧’, ‘⟦3⟧’, ‘⟦4⟧’, and ‘⟦5⟧’ lose their special meaning; instead use the backslashed versions ‘⟦6⟧’, ‘⟦7⟧’, ‘⟦8⟧’, ‘⟦9⟧’, ‘⟦10⟧’, and ‘⟦11⟧’. Also, a backslash is needed before an interval expression’s closing ‘⟦12⟧’.
units.sourceHTML: • The characters ‘?’, ‘+’, ‘{’, ‘|’, ‘(’, and ‘)’ lose their special meaning; instead use the backslashed versions ‘\?’, ‘\+’, ‘\{’, ‘\|’, ‘\(’, and ‘\)’. Also, a backslash is needed before an interval expression’s closing ‘}’.

units.text: If an unescaped ‘⟦0⟧’ appears neither first, nor directly after ‘⟦1⟧’ or ‘⟦2⟧’, it is treated like an ordinary character and is not an anchor.
units.sourceHTML: • If an unescaped ‘^’ appears neither first, nor directly after ‘\(’ or ‘\|’, it is treated like an ordinary character and is not an anchor.

units.text: If an unescaped ‘⟦0⟧’ appears neither last, nor directly before ‘⟦1⟧’ or ‘⟦2⟧’, it is treated like an ordinary character and is not an anchor.
units.sourceHTML: • If an unescaped ‘$’ appears neither last, nor directly before ‘\|’ or ‘\)’, it is treated like an ordinary character and is not an anchor.

units.text: If an unescaped ‘⟦0⟧’ appears first, or appears directly after ‘⟦1⟧’ or ‘⟦2⟧’ or anchoring ‘⟦3⟧’, it is treated like an ordinary character and is not a repetition operator.
units.sourceHTML: • If an unescaped ‘*’ appears first, or appears directly after ‘\(’ or ‘\|’ or anchoring ‘^’, it is treated like an ordinary character and is not a repetition operator.

nonProse: Command/flag literals and pure code/output examples retained; explanatory dt labels and italic pre descriptions extracted too; no unhandled prose text.
